page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a High Performance virtual server featuring 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 350 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results reveal a mix of performance characteristics. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25 percent. However, its Geekbench single-core and text processing scores fall into the bottom 25 percent. Multi-core performance across Geekbench, stress-ng, and Passmark CPU tests consistently registers in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, with read-only large block speeds at 84.3 GB/sec and write speeds at 63.29 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance handles 13.03 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and achieves average throughput in Passmark database operations.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies in the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce resource contention despite the high-performance AMD EPYC hardware. This shared model makes the instance a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high resource density and local NVMe storage without the premium of dedicated cores. It is well-suited for static web serving, software compilation, and light database operations, but less optimal for sustained high-compute tasks or medium-to-large language model inference.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance in stress-ng tests, while multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently perform in the average tier. However, Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are positioned in the lower tier. The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff in resource consistency, making this server a cost-efficient choice for workloads that benefit from fast local NVMe storage and multi-threaded capabilities without requiring dedicated CPU cores. It is suitable for static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database tasks.
